In this habilitation, I have demonstrated how decision analytical methods and probabilistic modeling provide structured approaches to address the complex challenges of agroecology and sustainable development. By systematically applying these techniques, I have identified key trade-offs, risks, and uncertainties that shape agricultural decision-making, policy design, and environmental management. These methods have allowed me to integrate expert knowledge, participatory insights, and probabilistic reasoning, ensuring that agroecological interventions are both scientifically robust and practically viable. In an era of escalating global change, these methodologies provide practical, scalable, and adaptive frameworks that support resilient food systems and informed decision-making across diverse agricultural landscapes. My work generates insights into how sustainable development can be achieved through transdisciplinary modeling, offering theoretical advances in decision theory and practical tools for policymakers. 

My research has shown that uncertainty is an inherent feature of agroecological systems, and decision-support tools must account for this variability. Through the application of Bayesian networks, Monte Carlo simulations, and structured decision analysis, I have refined methods for evaluating interventions under conditions of incomplete information. By combining these probabilistic models with stakeholder engagement and participatory frameworks, I have strengthened the alignment between scientific modeling and real-world agricultural realities, making decision-support tools more accessible and actionable.

While my work so far has mainly focused on case studies, the models are designed to be scalable and applicable to other regions facing similar challenges. The decision-support framework can be adapted to other contexts, allowing for global applications that are tailored to local conditions. This is particularly important for smallholder farmers and Indigenous communities, whose livelihoods are directly impacted by both climate change and conservation policies. I ensure that the solutions are locally grounded—reflecting the unique social, ecological, and economic conditions of each community. My work has the potential to make a lasting impact both at the local level, by improving livelihoods, and at the global level, by informing international development and conservation strategies.

## Contributions to Agroecology

My research has demonstrated how formal decision analysis improves the efficacy of agroecological interventions by structuring uncertainty, trade-offs, and stakeholder priorities into a coherent framework. By applying Bayesian networks, Monte Carlo simulations, and structured decision models, I have developed approaches that facilitate evidence-based decision-making and improve the practical applicability of agroecological strategies. These methods ensure that decision-support tools align with both scientific principles and local agricultural realities.

I have applied probabilistic tools to manage uncertainties in agricultural decision-making, illustrating how expert-elicited probabilities enhance policy and intervention assessments. By integrating stochastic models and scenario-based approaches, my work has supported resilient and adaptive agricultural strategies, providing quantitative insights into intervention outcomes and enabling stakeholders to make uncertainty-aware decisions in dynamic agroecosystems.

My research has also emphasized the importance of sustainable species prioritization, ecosystem management, and conservation planning in agroecological systems. Through allometric models, restoration simulations, and probabilistic assessments, I have quantified ecological trade-offs and benefits, helping guide conservation efforts, reforestation strategies, and agroforestry interventions. These contributions provide structured approaches to balancing biodiversity conservation with agricultural productivity, ensuring that sustainability remains central to agroecological decision-making.

## Future Research Directions

Looking forward, I aim to further advance transdisciplinary decision modeling to scale agroecological solutions and inform policy frameworks. The research will focus on refining hybrid models that integrate expert-elicited probabilities with emerging datasets, expanding multi-criteria decision analysis for more holistic trade-off assessments, and strengthening science-policy-practice networks to enhance the uptake of decision-support tools in real-world applications. By continuing to develop and refine probabilistic decision frameworks, I will contribute to better navigating the uncertainties of agricultural transitions, ensuring that sustainable development pathways remain resilient, equitable, and scientifically grounded.

My future research objectives are to develop scientifically grounded models that optimize human well-being and environmental sustainability interventions and apply these models to address region-specific challenges. I have applied for an ERC for work that will emphasize forecasting, scenario analysis, and the integration of local knowledge, leading to novel frameworks for balancing human welfare with ecological integrity. The results will offer insights and new approaches for how sustainable development is understood and practiced globally.

Future work will focus on refining decision models to better capture the dynamic and interconnected nature of agroecological systems. Integrating real-time data and improving the accuracy of probabilistic forecasts will enhance decision-making processes by providing more adaptive and context-specific insights. Expanding cross-disciplinary collaboration will be essential for developing holistic solutions, bringing together ecologists, social scientists, and economists to address both environmental and socio-economic challenges. Further research should also explore how to effectively scale agroecological practices while incorporating local knowledge and stakeholder priorities. Developing structured frameworks for engagement and co-designed interventions will ensure that agroecological transitions remain contextually relevant, scientifically robust, and socially equitable.

## Policy Implications

Policymakers should adopt decision analytical methods to design and evaluate agricultural policies, ensuring that interventions account for uncertainty, trade-offs, and stakeholder needs. The application of probabilistic decision models, as demonstrated in @fernandez_prioritizing_2022, provides a structured framework for identifying the most effective farm management interventions, allowing policymakers to optimize resource allocation and policy impact. Our work in @luu_decision_2022 further highlights how stakeholder-driven agro-climate services can be scaled more effectively when policy frameworks integrate expert-elicited knowledge and participatory decision-making.

Supporting agroecological transitions requires targeted policies that prioritize investments in sustainable farming systems, particularly in climate-vulnerable regions. Research such as @do_decision_2020, which applied participatory modeling with Vietnamese smallholder farmers, underscores the need for policies that align with local farming realities by integrating farmer knowledge into agroforestry adoption frameworks. @oluoch_indigenous_2023 further demonstrates how policies that incorporate Indigenous ecological knowledge can enhance conservation efforts and agroforestry management, ensuring that interventions remain socially and culturally relevant.

The findings of my work underscore the transformative potential of combining decision analysis with agroecological principles. As the global community seeks sustainable solutions to environmental and food system challenges, these decision-support frameworks provide a robust foundation for guiding policies that benefit both people and ecosystems. By embedding probabilistic reasoning, participatory engagement, and sustainability considerations into policy design, governments and organizations can create adaptive, data-driven strategies that support resilient agroecological transitions.
